M6.head: M6 · Housing supply + composition
M6.actw: ACTW: 12,000+ homes by 2030 with composition targets: 25% missing middle, 20% 3BR+, 15% non-market, 30% rental. Quarterly reporting on each

Al.text: "Unlock more homes." Volume committed; no published composition targets, no quarterly reporting

Ca.text: Drafted the Sept 2023 Missing Middle overhaul — dropped bonus-density costs, raised heights, livable basements plus 3 storeys. Council adopted the city's first family housing policy, a composition instrument (Vic News Dec 21 2025)

De.text: "7000+ units approved this term." Strong volume advocacy, no composition discipline

Th.text: Pro-supply; eliminate parking minimums. A real instrument, not a composition one

Ki.text: Non-market, public and co-op emphasis aligning on M6's 15% non-market line (2022 platform)

Lo.text: Pro-supply. STEP addresses throughput, not new-construction composition

Co.text: Recorded NO, Jan 2023 and the Sept 2023 overhaul. Process objections rather than principle

Ga.text: Recorded NO; demanded the MNP governance review first

Cs.text: No position on volume or composition. "Results over ideology" is not a housing position; the inference note was removed in v1.8

Ro.text: No position on volume or composition. Affordability named as a campaign pillar

Bo.text: "Housing that fits into complete communities" (Vic News May 15 2026), against a documented critique: ~518 units/yr for five years in a 2 km² neighbourhood, ~5,500 more in the pipeline, no amenities beyond two public toilets (@wdbowkett 2024). The closest published analogue on the field to ACTW's composition-and-amenity argument. No target named, so 🟡

Mc.text: "More Missing Middle housing: townhouses, multiplexes, courtyard housing" (arthurmcinnis.ca) — the composition mix M6 targets. Found July 30; this page previously recorded him as having none

Le.text: "Encourage the building of 3 & 4 bedroom units, so families have space to live" — the M6 20% 3BR+ composition line with a named direction — plus "Build affordable housing" and "More purpose built co-ops and below market housing" (bellalee.ca/policy, read July 31 2026). No numeric target

Sa.text: "Build more housing of all kinds, especially deeply affordable housing"; "Make it easier to build family suitable housing… keep families in Victoria" (jacksandor.ca/platform, read July 31 2026). Family-suitable and non-market composition directions named; no numeric target

M6b.head: M6b · City land bank + co-operative housing
M6b.actw: ACTW: A City land bank acquiring and holding land for non-market and affordable delivery

Al.text: City land bank, 2022 platform. Absorbed as M6b in v1.2

Mc.text: "Greater use of co-operative housing and city-owned land to create homes for working families, seniors, and young people" (arthurmcinnis.ca). Same asset, different vehicle

Le.text: "More purpose built co-ops and below market housing. Including making it easier to form a housing co-op"; empty lots and derelict buildings turned into affordable housing (bellalee.ca/policy). Co-op delivery named; a different vehicle than a land bank

Sa.text: "Pilot a city financing program for co-op housing, to increase the diversity and affordability of housing" (jacksandor.ca/platform). Co-op delivery via city financing — same asset class, different vehicle

M7.head: M7 · Permits + AI pre-screening
M7.actw: ACTW: Published targets by category (simple <6 weeks, complex <6 months, rezoning <9 months); AI pre-screening on the Kelowna KAI model; one-stop development centre; quarterly variance reports

Al.text: No published permit-time benchmarks during four years in office

De.text: "The epitome of bad governance is the failure to make a decision" (Capital Daily). Process critic, no permit mechanism

Ha.text: General "reduce red tape" posture; no benchmark mechanism

Ga.text: General "reduce red tape" posture; no benchmark mechanism

Cs.text: The "predictability, order, and trust" quote is about public safety, not permitting. Adjacency is not a source. Downgraded from 🟡 in v1.8

Ro.text: No public position on permit processing

Bo.text: No public position on permit processing

Mc.text: Same policy area, opposite direction. Infrastructure reviews tied to development approvals adds a condition where M7 compresses. He has not published his reasoning and it should be asked rather than assumed

Sa.text: No public position. A Red Seal electrician who has pulled permits — background, not a position

M7b.head: M7b · Pre-approved pattern-book housing *(v1.9)*
M7b.actw: ACTW: Municipal pattern book for duplex, triplex, fourplex, townhouse, courtyard and laneway forms, with an automatic expedited permit stream at the M7 simple-permit target

Ca.text: No public position. He drafted the Missing Middle overhaul and proposes no pattern book

Mc.text: "Streamlining approvals for appropriate infill through tools such as pattern books and pre-approved designs" (arthurmcinnis.ca). The mechanism named almost verbatim

Sa.text: No public position. He has built the forms in question and proposes no pattern book

M8 / M8b.head: M8 / M8b · DCC reductions for rental; suite legalization amnesty *(M8b v1.9)*
M8 / M8b.actw: ACTW: Targeted DCC reductions for purpose-built rental (M8); a 24-month life-safety-only amnesty for existing unpermitted secondary suites with a named concierge and tenant protection against eviction and rent reset (M8b)

Sa.text: "Permanently exempt nonmarket housing from all taxes, charges, and fees, to get as much deeply affordable housing as possible built as quickly as possible" (jacksandor.ca/platform, read July 31 2026). The same fee-relief lever as M8, aimed at non-market rather than purpose-built rental. The first candidate in the field with a position on this cluster

M9 / M9b / M64.head: M9 / M9b / M64 · Tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated)
M9 / M9b / M64.actw: ACTW: STR licensing tightening (M9b); vacancy-control-between-tenancies advocacy (M9c); 26°C maximum-temperature rental bylaw (M64)

Al.text: Rent banks (2022 plank) and the 2026 rental-support motion. No STR tightening, no heat-bylaw position

Ca.text: Co-author of the May 2026 cooling bylaw motion, 26°C, New Westminster precedent

De.text: Co-author of the May 2026 cooling bylaw motion

Th.text: Co-author of the cooling bylaw motion; "decades of tight restrictions on building new rentals led to rock bottom vacancy rates"

Ki.text: Vacancy control between tenancies and AirBnB licensing tightening, 2022 planks absorbed as M9c and M9b. Conceptually ahead of the 2026 motion

Ha.text: Tenant Resource and Advisory Centre board member — background, not a position. No STR or heat-bylaw position

Cs.text: No public position on these mechanisms

Mc.text: No public position. Tenant protection appears in his platform pillars; scored under M6 rather than here

Le.text: "Support Renters… If a landlord refuses to make a repair, the City will do it and send them the bill with a 25% service tax"; "Allow pets in rentals" (bellalee.ca/policy, read July 31 2026). A named tenant-protection enforcement mechanism, different from the Renters' Hub. No STR or heat-bylaw position

Sa.text: "Increase funding for the Greater Victoria Rent Bank, to keep people housed" (jacksandor.ca/platform, read July 31 2026). A named tenant-stability funding instrument. No STR or heat-bylaw position

M10.head: M10 · Transparent algorithmic waitlist allocation
M10.actw: ACTW: Transparent, points-based, publicly auditable allocation for subsidized housing waitlists

M11.head: M11 · Homelessness — Housing First + STEP throughput
M11.actw: ACTW: 50% reduction in unsheltered homelessness via Housing-First plus STEP-style throughput (Loughton motion absorbed); capacity-first enforcement (M35); 89% regional burden flagged for fair-share advocacy

Al.text: Convened the 11-member Community Leaders Panel and initiated the CSWB plan, adopted July 3 2025 (City of Victoria). Authoring a plan is naming an instrument. Admits "it took nearly a year before council's focus turned to community safety"

Ca.text: Caledonia Place regional fair-share motion with Hammond — "the city for too long has done it all"

Th.text: Co-author, Coordinated Access & Assessment downtown prioritization motion, June 2025 — the intake-side complement to STEP

Ki.text: Pro-supportive-housing. Lone NO on the July 2024 sheltering ban (scored under M33)

Lo.text: STEP (Supporting Tenants, Enabling Pathways) motion originator, Jan 2026. Measure 11 absorbs her work directly

Co.text: CSWB supporter; NO on Dowler Place zoning

Ha.text: Daytime sheltering ban author (July 2024, passed 8–1). Capacity-first sequencing aligns directly

Ga.text: Five Pillars approach — prevention, harm reduction, treatment, enforcement, housing

Cs.text: "Supportive of capacity-first frame" was inference. Downgraded from 🟡 in v1.8. No position on Housing First, throughput or enforcement sequencing

Ro.text: No public position on homelessness policy

Bo.text: No public position. Board member of The Soup Kitchen — background, not a position, banned inference 5

Mc.text: No public position on homelessness policy

Le.text: "Create a housing liaison to help folks get out of transitional housing" — STEP throughput in substance — plus "Work with the Province to create more treatment beds" and "Support harm reduction, and safe supply" (bellalee.ca/policy, read July 31 2026)

Sa.text: "Increase assistance for people moving through supportive housing, to make better use of our limited resources" — the STEP throughput argument, rationale included — plus displacement-reducing zoning changes (jacksandor.ca/platform, read July 31 2026)

M12 / M13b / M13c.head: M12 / M13b / M13c · Childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is $0 → M13d)
M12 / M13b / M13c.actw: ACTW: Advocate 500 new childcare spaces (M12); school food quality with SD61 (M13); family-doctor recruitment via low or no-rent clinic space plus permissive tax exemption (M13b); reach young adults 18–25 (M13c)

Al.text: Housing and practice incentives for health professionals, and permissive tax exemptions for not-for-profit clinics — both 2022 planks, both absorbed into M13b

Ca.text: No public position on any of the four

Ki.text: No public position. Fernwood NRG role is community-services background, not a position — banned inference 5

Mc.text: No public position on the family and school cluster

Le.text: "Build purpose-built housing for doctors and nurse practitioners in return for a practice in Victoria"; "Create a city owned walk in clinic" — Colwood named as the model (bellalee.ca/policy, read July 31 2026). Comparable instruments to M13b's clinic-space-plus-tax-exemption. Her MCFD background note is superseded: she now has a published municipal position

Sa.text: "Build a municipal clinic, following the success of Colwood and Langford, to attract more family doctors" (jacksandor.ca/platform, read July 31 2026). A comparable instrument to M13b

M13d.head: M13d · Standing School District 61 agreement *(v1.8)*
M13d.actw: ACTW: A standing agreement with SD61 — joint use of gyms, fields and playgrounds; safe routes to school as a programme rather than a complaint line; childcare on school sites

Al.text: "Enhanced use of Royal Athletic Park, including SD61, community organizations' programs, and public access" (altomayor.ca). A named partner on one facility, not a standing agreement

Sa.text: "Work with school districts and other organizations to use underutilized spaces like school gyms for arts and culture events" (jacksandor.ca/platform, read July 31 2026). The joint-use component of M13d, arts-scoped; not a standing agreement

M14 / M16 / M17 / M18.head: M14 / M16 / M17 / M18 · Cleanliness and the public realm
M14 / M16 / M17 / M18.actw: ACTW: 90% of graffiti removed within 48 hours, published quarterly with median report-to-removal time (M14); pest and rodent plan (M16); extended sanitation hours (M17); public art on repeatedly tagged surfaces from the existing $207K budget (M18)

Al.text: Expanded public-realm cleaning, bylaw presence and ambassadors (2022 platform); OUR DWTN funds enhanced downtown cleaning. No service standard and no published metric, which is the whole of M14

Ca.text: No public position on a cleanliness standard

De.text: OUR DWTN at $1M annual is his named plank and enhanced cleaning sits inside it. A funded named programme. No standard, cadence or published metric

Ha.text: No public position on a cleanliness standard

Ga.text: Cleanliness leads her own 2022 framing: "Victoria would be so much cleaner and inviting, so much safer and prosperous, if the well-being and interests of those who live here become Council's priorities." No standard or mechanism

Cs.text: Not yet published. Her experience as a downtown business owner is background, not a position

Bo.text: "They want safe streets, reliable services, well-maintained parks and roads" (Vic News May 15 2026). Service-basics commitment; no standard or metric

Le.text: "Continue to fund the Downtown Victoria Business Association to support local businesses with graffiti removal and facade repairs", plus "caring about the little things like garbage and recycling being picked up on time" (bellalee.ca/policy, read July 31 2026). A funded removal channel; no service standard or published metric, which is the whole of M14

M19 / M22 / M38 / M40–42b.head: M19 / M22 / M38 / M40–42b · Mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38)
M19 / M22 / M38 / M40–42b.actw: ACTW: Adaptive traffic signals on major corridors (Pittsburgh SURTRAC model); Vision Zero 50% reduction by 2030 (Hoboken benchmark); first-hour free parking; Westshore E&N advocacy; federal hood-height advocacy (M42b)

Al.text: "Reimagine transportation" plank. No Vision Zero target, no adaptive-signal commitment

De.text: Pro-bike; AI consultation imagery for park redesigns (scored under M53)

Th.text: Hoboken Vision Zero benchmark cited publicly — the same peer-city evidence ACTW uses. Eliminate parking minimums; e-bike rebates

Ki.text: Bike valet expansion; reduce parking minimums

Ha.text: General "core services" posture; no specific mobility position

Cs.text: "I want to make the streets accessible again" (CHEK News). Sourced on the area, no mechanism

Ro.text: "Remove the barriers stopping people from coming downtown and restore the vibrant downtown that has been lost" (karenrothe.ca)

Bo.text: Corrected July 31 (audit ③): the "well-maintained parks and roads" clause is road maintenance and is scored under M25. Road maintenance is not Vision Zero

Mc.text: "They can't find parking, they can't get where they want to go quickly" (Vic News June 25 2026). Parking availability and travel time are precisely what M19 and M24 target. No mechanism named

Le.text: "Expand Fare Free transit to seniors"; "Advocate for lower bus fees" (bellalee.ca/policy, read July 31 2026). Named transit-advocacy instruments; no Vision Zero target or signal position

Sa.text: "Prepare for rail transit on Douglas street"; "Increase traffic enforcement, to keep our roads safe for everyone"; "Increase the amount of accessible street parking downtown" (jacksandor.ca/platform, read July 31 2026). Named instruments — enforcement-led rather than signal-led on safety; no Vision Zero target

M20b / M23b.head: M20b / M23b · Walking, and transit — what the City actually controls *(v1.8)*
M20b / M23b.actw: ACTW: Walking: published sidewalk gap inventory, annual km closed, crossing-spacing standard, pedestrian signal timing at real walking speeds. Transit: a named transit-priority capital line; a published City transit position; a published record of how Victoria's Regional Transit Commission representatives voted; local share bounded by the M66 cap. Explicitly no promises on routes or fares

Al.text: "Reimagine transportation" is a declared 2026 plank. No jurisdictional line, no capital figure, no sidewalk commitment

Ca.text: Advanced a new CRD transportation service as CRD vice-chair (Vic News Dec 21 2025). An act on regional service delivery, not the seat

De.text: No specific walking or transit-funding position

Th.text: Protected bike-and-roll peer-city benchmarking against Saanich, Esquimalt, Edmonton, Minneapolis, Chicago, Austin, Boston, Nashville and Ann Arbor — a named method matching ACTW's own. Cycling-led rather than walking-led

Ki.text: Bike valet expansion; reduce parking minimums; car-share and e-bike incentives

Cs.text: "I want to make the streets accessible again" (CHEK News). Detailed platform pending

Ro.text: Names transit among core local-government responsibilities: "infrastructure, transportation, public safety, affordability, and public transportation systems that work for all" (karenrothe.ca). No mechanism or jurisdictional distinction

Bo.text: Corrected July 31 (audit ③): the entry's own text said the clause "is road maintenance (M25) rather than walking or transit." Scored under M25 only

Mc.text: Transportation one of five named platform areas. No mechanism

Le.text: "Bike lane improvements and connecting bike lanes to other municipalities"; "Build more bus shelters" (bellalee.ca/policy, read July 31 2026). Named city-controlled instruments; no sidewalk inventory, no transit-vote publication position

Sa.text: The flagged weakest-🟡 is resolved exactly as directed — a published statement now exists. "Build more Bike Valets, and extend their hours, to reduce bike theft and make cycling more convenient" (jacksandor.ca/platform, read July 31 2026). The BetterTransitYYJ board seat reverts to background

M24b / M25b.head: M24b / M25b · Accessibility and public washrooms
M24b / M25b.actw: ACTW: Public washrooms treated as transportation infrastructure, 24/7 network, $400–600K/yr (M24b, absorbing Coun. Kim's 2022 plank); universal accessibility audit and remediation of every sidewalk, public building, washroom and transit-adjacent site, with a Disability Advisory Committee (M25b)

Al.text: No public position on an accessibility audit or a washroom network

Ki.text: Public bathrooms as transportation infrastructure is her own 2022 plank, absorbed as M24b. She named both the mechanism and the framing, and the framing is the substantive part: treating washrooms as infrastructure rather than amenity is what makes them fundable from a transportation line. The clearest single case of ACTW adopting a sitting progressive councillor's idea outright

Ha.text: No public position. Board service with the Western Institute for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing is background, not a position — banned inference 5, applied here exactly as it was to Bowkett's Soup Kitchen service

Cs.text: Not yet published. "Make the streets accessible again" is scored under mobility; it is about access to downtown rather than disability accessibility

Bo.text: No public position. She notes her neighbourhood received "two public toilets" as the sum of amenity investment, which is a criticism of amenity delivery rather than a washroom commitment

Sa.text: "Build more public washrooms, and better maintain the ones we already have, to keep our streets clean and improve accessibility", and "Increase the amount of accessible street parking downtown… for people with disabilities" (jacksandor.ca/platform, read July 31 2026). The M24b mechanism named without the transportation-infrastructure framing that is Kim's ✅; accessibility direction on M25b without the audit instrument

M25.head: M25 · Fix roads first
M25.actw: ACTW: Road and sidewalk maintenance prioritized ahead of discretionary capital

Bo.text: "Safe streets, reliable services, well-maintained parks and roads" (Vic News May 15 2026). Sourced on the area, no standard or budget line
